body: Rising consumer prices have intensified pressure on the Federal Reserve to tighten monetary policy, after US inflation accelerated to 3.8% in October. The Commerce Department released the figures Wednesday, November 25, 2026, showing persistent price increases across the economy as policymakers prepare for their December interest rate decision. According to the latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) report, annual headline inflation increased from 3.6% in September to 3.8% in October, matching economists' expectations. The reading marked the highest level in five months and stood nearly twice the Federal Reserve's 2% inflation target. Core PCE, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, climbed to 3.3% annually from 3.1% in September. That exceeded the 3.2% forecast by 0.1 percentage point, according to the Commerce Department. Monthly headline and core inflation both increased 0.3%. The report also showed personal income rising 0.7%, exceeding the 0.4% forecast, while consumer spending increased 0.3%. The personal saving rate reached 4.1%. Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh previously emphasized the central bank's responsibility to control rising prices while policymakers assessed economic conditions and employment trends. "It's our responsibility to get inflation down," Warsh said at a press conference in Washington, D.C. Economic growth has provided additional evidence of resilient demand. A revised Commerce Department estimate showed gross domestic product expanding at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter. Consumer spending increased 4.2% during the quarter, while real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 5.8%. Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds, warned that strong economic demand could complicate efforts to control inflation. "Inflation is too hot and it will not be brought under control as long as economic demand is also too hot," Rupkey said. Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, also highlighted inflationary pressures extending beyond energy costs. "America's inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock," Long said. Higher energy costs followed the outbreak of the Iran war in late February, disrupting global oil supplies. Tariffs and strong demand associated with artificial intelligence investment have also contributed to price pressures, according to the economic reports. Bradley Saunders, an economist at Capital Economics, said the underlying inflation figures strengthened the case for additional monetary tightening. "The continued strength in core PCE inflation … make[s] a December rate hike certain," Saunders said. He added that a further increase in January could become necessary. However, Mike Skordeles, head of US economics at Truist Advisory Services, offered a more measured assessment, pointing to comparisons with relatively low inflation readings from the previous year. "The overall inflation trajectory is largely unchanged, especially when excluding food and energy," Skordeles said. Federal Reserve Governor Chris Waller has argued that a December quarter-point increase should be accompanied by a signal of another increase in January, or replaced with a larger half-percentage-point move. Governor Lisa Cook has also warned that delaying action could leave policymakers behind inflation. Financial markets have largely anticipated a 0.25-percentage-point increase at the Federal Reserve's December 8-9 meeting. However, expectations for further increases in 2027 remain less certain. According to CME Group's FedWatch Tool, traders reduced the probability of a third additional increase in 2027 to approximately one-third, compared with roughly 50% the previous day. Meanwhile, Labor Department data showed initial jobless claims falling to 189,000 for the week ending November 21, down 13,000 from the previous week and below the 200,000 economists had expected.

title: Gold prices drop another 1% as US Q3 GDP revised to 4.3% with contained PCE inflation - Kitco
body: (Kitco News) - Solid economic growth in the third quarter and contained inflation pressures have pushed gold prices back below what some analysts have said is a key support level. The Bureau of Economic Analysis announced that the preliminary reading of third-quarter Gross Domestic Product showed the economy grew 4.3% between July and September, up from the initial estimate of 3.4% and up from 2.2% in the second quarter. The data was better than economists expected, as consensus forecasts were looking for a growth rate of 3.5%. “The contributors to the increase in real GDP in the third quarter were increases in investment, consumer spending, and government spending that were partly offset by a decrease in exports. Imports, which are a subtraction in the calculation of GDP, increased,” the report said. “Real GDP was revised up 0.9 percentage point from the advance estimate, primarily reflecting upward revisions to investment and consumer spending.” While the U.S. economy continues to expand, the report noted that inflation pressures appear to be restrained. The report said that the price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7% in the third quarter, down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate. Meanwhile, the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index for the quarter increased 2.1%, and the PCE price index excluding food and energy increased 2.5%, both unchanged from the initial estimate. In a separate report, the BEA noted that general inflation pressures remain contained heading into the fourth quarter. The core PCE price index, which strips out volatile food and energy prices, rose 0.3% in October, in line with economists’ expectations. The report said that over the last 12 months, the PCE price index increased 3.8%, up from 3.6% in September. Annual core PCE increased 3.3%, up from 3.1%. Although inflation pressures remain elevated, analysts note that they are not accelerating. However, the data still provides no support for gold, as it gives the Federal Reserve room to raise interest rates next month and in early 2027. The gold market was already seeing solid selling pressure, trading near $3,500 ahead of the latest U.S. economic data. The yellow metal has been unable to hold that critical support level following the solid third-quarter economic data and in-line inflation numbers. Spot gold last traded at $3,484.20 an ounce, down nearly 2% on the day. Although activity in the third quarter was stronger than expected, Nidal Abdel Hadi, CEO of Finoro, said that the data is significantly backward-looking. “The third quarter turned out to be a blowout, with growth smashing forecasts while the broad price gauge cooled and core PCE ticked along on script. But that’s a story about the summer,” Hadi said. “Monday’s softer services survey and the steady drift higher in jobless claims say momentum has faded since, leaving the Fed with a stellar report card for a term that has already ended.” Chris Zaccarelli, Chief Investment Officer for Northlight Asset Management, said that although inflation is not accelerating, it is still too high and is unlikely to convince the Fed to remain on hold. title: Bank of Canada expected to hike interest rate next month, economists say - Global News
body: Some Canadians could see their finances tighten more as economists say they expect the Bank of Canada to increase its key interest rate again next month. The prediction comes after they say the central bank’s governor, Tiff Macklem, warned Tuesday that cost pressures are building on businesses. “We thought that there might be an opening where the Bank of Canada could delay the next interest rate increase into early next year,” said Sal Guatieri, BMO Capital Markets senior economist. “But that seemed to just go out the window with the governor basically just confirming that the bank is still quite concerned about energy costs pass-through to the broader measures of inflation.” Guatieri said Canadians could see at least a 0.25 basis point increase, bringing the key interest rate to 2.75 per cent. During his speech at the Economic Club of Canada, Macklem spoke of ongoing economic “shocks” and said that while oil prices and refinery margins have dropped, inflation is expected to persist. He also predicted a “second-round effect of the oil shock” will add to that in the new year. Guatieri added that with the governor still describing the economy as “resilient,” and its goal to get inflation under control, another hike is likely needed. The Bank of Canada is expected to deliver its next rate decision on Dec. 9 — its last of 2026. It announced a rate hike of 0.25 basis points on Oct. 28, bringing the policy rate to 2.5 per cent – the first time it had raised the rate in more than three years. At the time, Macklem said the decision was an effort to prevent higher energy prices from spreading to the prices of other goods and services. It was also seen as a response to pressure the bank faced due to the Iran war and other geopolitical conflicts resulting in higher prices for oil and gas. Macklem said Tuesday that when disruptions, such as to oil markets, push prices up without slowing economic growth, it can cause higher prices for households. When this happens, along with worse job prospects, the central bank has to weigh the risk of ongoing inflation with the possibility of weakening the economy with further interest rate changes. “The best contribution monetary policy can make to the well-being of Canadians is to keep inflation low, stable and predictable,” said Macklem. Though he stressed the economy was showing resilience, CIBC Chief Economist Avery Shenfeld said they’ve seen it weaken. “That still leaves us now thinking that he wants to raise interest rates sooner than later rather than wait and see another month or two,” Shenfeld said. With the potential for businesses that have shouldered the increased costs of transportation and production for some time to start passing those higher costs down to consumers, the bank is likely to take action again. According to Shenfeld though, December might be where the rate hikes stop – at least for now. “We don’t expect this inflation outburst to last too long, and we don’t expect to see a lot of interest rate hikes either,” he said. “We expect that December hike to be the last one we’ll see for quite a while.” Even if a rate hike is expected in an effort to battle back persistent inflation, Guatieri cautions the Bank of Canada from doing so. He said if the economy is weaker than expected, there’s a softer labour market and if unemployment continues to rise, interest rate hikes could have a heavier affect. That stands more true if a trade deal — even an interim one — isn’t reached with the U.S. and more tariffs come into effect in January. “It could end up being premature and who knows, the bank may end up having to reverse these rate increases if the economy softens through the next year,” Guatieri said.

title: S&P warns Nvidia credit rating could be cut over 'rising' management and governance risk
summary: S&P Global Ratings said Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch as it flagged "rising" management and governance risk at the chipmaker.
body: Nvidia's credit rating could be cut by one notch over the next 90 days if the company continues to have "deficiencies" in its management and governance framework, S&P Global Ratings said in the wake of the Jensen Huang's ouster and reinstatement as Nvidia CEO. "News regarding the CEO and questions regarding potential export control violations have exposed vulnerabilities in Nvidia's management and governance framework, especially in regard to its board structure, composition, and effectiveness," S&P said in a Wednesday note . Nvidia currently holds an AA rating, the third-highest level. S&P has placed the chipmaker on "CreditWatch with negative implications," though any potential downgrade would be limited to one notch, to AA-, unless investigations or disclosures lead the agency to conclude that Nvidia's reputation or future prospects have also been harmed. A downgrade can pressure bond prices, push yields higher and raise borrowing costs. Nvidia priced $25 billion of investment-grade senior notes in June, with maturities from 2028 through 2056, shortly after S&P upgraded the company from AA- to AA. Nvidia has about $32.5 billion of bonds in the U.S. high-grade corporate bond index, according to Bloomberg. S&P's Wednesday note follows Moody's Ratings changing its outlook on Nvidia to stable from positive on Nov. 18, citing governance concerns, and leaving that outlook unchanged after Huang's return on Monday. In its note, S&P cited the "long tenure" of certain board members as a reason their independence may be "compromised" and said Nvidia's management and governance risk was "rising." The ratings agency added that it remained unaware of any remedial action taken by the board to address what could be "meaningful" management and governance deficiencies. Chairman Harvey Jones and early investor Tench Coxe have served on Nvidia's board since 1993, while Brooke Seawell joined in 1997. Mark Stevens served from 1993 to 2006 and rejoined the board in 2008. S&P also flagged questions around geopolitical risk management and internal controls arising from Nvidia's exposure to China. "While Nvidia management has delivered significant returns for its stakeholders over decades, weak executive oversight and lack of succession planning have brought questions around the "key man" risk to the forefront," S&P's Andrew Chang and David Tsui said. Chang and Tsui noted that Huang's resignation and subsequent reinstatement did not resolve questions about the board's oversight of executive conduct. The agency also intends to meet with Nvidia's board and management to discuss plans to address those deficiencies, particularly around "board independence, effective management oversight and a credible leadership succession plan." Huang returned less than two weeks after Jones said Nvidia's directors did not intend to reinstate him. The board later voted unanimously to bring Huang back, sending Nvidia shares up as much as 36% during Monday's session.

body: The surprise is large, but the market reaction is likely to stay muted because so much of the spending is imported equipment that does little for local output or wages. Investors are more likely to focus on what it says about capacity pressure and the RBA's December decision, where any lift in hike odds would support the Australian dollar and push up short-term yields. The industry mix matters for equities: the boom is concentrated in data centres and technology rather than mining, which favours data centre operators, construction and electrical contractors, and power suppliers over the resources sector that dominated past investment cycles. Australia's investment boom is back near mining-boom highs, but this time it's being built from server racks rather than iron ore mines. Australian business investment surged far beyond expectations in the third quarter. Private capital spending jumped 12.2% from the previous quarter, almost three times the 4.4% rise economists had forecast, Australian Bureau of Statistics data showed on Thursday. The figures, released at 0030 GMT (1930 US Eastern on Wednesday), put total capex at about A$59.5 billion for the quarter in inflation-adjusted terms, 18.6% higher than a year earlier. That takes it close to the peak reached during the mining investment boom more than a decade ago. The jump came almost entirely from equipment. Spending on plant and machinery soared 23.1% in the quarter and 34.3% from a year earlier, reversing an 8.9% fall in the June quarter and lifting it to a record. Investment in buildings and structures rose a more modest 1.7%. The industry detail points clearly to data centres. Total investment in information media and telecommunications, the industry that includes data centres, rose 86.7% in the quarter, and its equipment spending nearly tripled, up 183.5%. Earlier this year the ABS attributed a 6.5% jump in March-quarter capex to data centre equipment such as server racks and processing gear, and the June-quarter fall was widely seen as payback. Mining investment rose just 1.4%, while non-mining capex climbed 16.0%. Victoria led the states with a 31.0% rise. Firms also plan to keep spending. Their fourth estimate of capital expenditure for the 2026-27 financial year came in at about A$224 billion, 11.8% above the previous estimate. Planned equipment spending was revised up 20.4% to about A$102 billion, far outpacing a 5.6% upgrade for buildings and structures. There is an important caveat. Much of that equipment is imported , so a large share of the spending flows offshore rather than adding to domestic output. The boost to Australia's GDP will therefore be considerably smaller than the headline suggests. The ABS also completed its annual seasonal review with this release, which caused minor revisions to the equipment series. For the Reserve Bank of Australia, the data still adds to the case that the economy is running hot. The RBA raised its cash rate to 4.85% on November 3, its highest since 2008 and its fifth hike of the year, in a split 6-3 vote. The board said inflation remains broad-based and likely to stay above 3% for longer than previously expected, but it dropped its explicit warning about further increases. The RBA's final meeting of the year concludes on December 8, with the decision due at 0330 GMT (2230 US Eastern on December 7). October inflation data and third-quarter GDP figures will carry more weight before then, but strong investment intentions make it harder for the board to argue that demand is cooling. The figures also stand out against a global backdrop of growing resistance to data centre projects , from Tokyo's suburbs to Australia's own Northern Territory. The stock subsequently fell to approximately $80 during pre-market trading as losses across cryptocurrency markets erased gains associated with the Nvidia rally. Data published by Strategy shows its multiple of net asset value (mNAV) at 0.97x, meaning its market valuation represents a 3% discount to the net asset value of its 851,305 BTC holdings. title: Bank of America 2027 Economic Outlook: AI Investment as the Top US Economy Uncertainty, Fed Projected to Hike Interest Rates 3 More Times - 36Kr
body: Bank of America believes that although the U.S. economy still shows strong resilience at present, the trend of the artificial intelligence (AI) investment wave may determine the trajectory of the U.S. economy and monetary policy in the next two years. If corporate investment continues to grow at a high speed, the Federal Reserve may have to raise the policy rate to 5% or even higher; once AI capital expenditure slows down sharply, the U.S. economy will face a higher risk of recession, and the Federal Reserve may also shift to interest rate cuts. A research report titled "2027 U.S. Economic Outlook" released by BofA Global Research on November 24 points out that supported by corporate investment and household consumption, the U.S. real GDP is expected to grow by 2.3% and 2.1% respectively in 2027 and 2028, but inflation will still be higher than the Federal Reserve's target. The bank expects the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates by 25 basis points at each of the next three meetings, and the AI capital expenditure cycle is the biggest uncertainty facing the above forecast. Bank of America believes that the economies of scale characteristics of the AI industry are prone to "rational overinvestment". In the end, only a few enterprises in this field may win, but every enterprise has to invest on the assumption that it will be the winner . Even if the investment decision of a single enterprise is reasonable, overinvestment may still occur in the whole industry. The most critical issue at present is when this capital expenditure cycle will turn. According to Bank of America's calculations, since the first quarter of 2025, the real annualized growth rate of AI-related capital expenditure sub-items in the United States, such as software, data centers, computers and peripheral equipment, is about 26%. (Since the first quarter of 2025, the real annualized growth rate of U.S. AI-related capital expenditure sub-items is about 26%. The chart shows the contribution of software, data centers, computers and peripheral equipment to investment growth) There are two completely different interpretations of this high growth rate: first, the overall scale of the AI investment wave exceeds previous expectations; second, a large amount of investment is implemented in advance, which means that future capital expenditure may decline sharply earlier and the decline will be more severe. Bank of America believes that recent economic data is not enough to judge which situation is closer to reality. Under the baseline scenario, Bank of America expects corporate investment to remain strong at least in the first half of 2027, and then gradually slow down. The growth rate of U.S. real non-residential investment is expected to drop from 7.6% in 2026 to 7.0% in 2027, and further drop to 2.9% in 2028. Calculated at the quarterly annualized rate, the non-residential investment growth rate is expected to drop from 6.3% in the first quarter of 2027 to 2.9% in the fourth quarter, and remain at 2.3% in all quarters of 2028. The bank did not include the scenario of investment shrinkage in the baseline forecast, mainly because it is difficult to judge when it will occur. Bank of America believes that the results of the U.S. mid-term elections will not significantly change its capital expenditure outlook. Even if some state governments introduce measures to slow down data center construction, the new regulations will take time to affect economic activities, and avoiding excessive advance of investment may instead reduce the risk of future economic recession . Bank of America also pointed out that due to the time lag between enterprises issuing investment guidelines and related changes being reflected in GDP data, the financial market may price in advance before the actual sharp decline in capital expenditure, but it may also send false signals many times during the period. title: U.S. Core PCE Inflation Hits 3.3%, Fed Seen Raising Rates in December and January - Businesskorea
body: With inflationary pressures in the United States remaining elevated, the Federal Reserve (Fed) is expected to raise interest rates in January, following a hike in December, according to an outlook from an iM Securities economist. In a report issued on Nov. 26, Park Sang-hyun, an economist at iM Securities, highlighted the 3.8% year-on-year increase in the U.S. Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index in October. The index also rose 0.3% from the previous month. Of particular note, the core PCE price index, which excludes food and energy and is closely watched by the Fed in setting monetary policy, increased 3.3% year on year, exceeding the market consensus of 3.2%. This marked its highest level since November 2023, underscoring persistent inflationary pressures. The so-called supercore PCE, which measures services prices excluding housing and energy, also rose 3.6%, indicating that inflationary pressures in the services sector remained elevated. Park said the inflation trend had effectively cemented the case for a Fed rate hike in December. He forecast that the Fed would raise its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to a range of 4.00% to 4.25% in December, followed by another 25-basis-point increase in January, bringing the range to 4.25% to 4.50%. CME FedWatch, as cited in the report, also pointed to a 98.1% probability of a December hike and a 59.7% chance of a January increase at the time. However, the probability of another hike in March stood at 36.5%, suggesting that the policy path beyond January remained uncertain. Despite elevated inflation and interest rates, U.S. corporate investment has remained stronger than expected. The U.S. economy grew at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, revised upward by 0.9 percentage points from the initial estimate of 3.4%. This was the fastest pace of growth since the third quarter of 2023. Nonresidential fixed investment, a measure of business spending, surged at an annualized rate of 16%, contributing 2.22 percentage points to overall GDP growth. Orders for nondefense capital goods excluding aircraft also rose 1.2% month on month in October, well above the market forecast of 0.7%. The increase suggests that corporate investment plans remain solid. The recent sharp decline in AI- and semiconductor-related stocks could also become a factor in the Fed's monetary policy decisions. Park said equity markets were pressuring the Fed to avoid excessive tightening, adding that the central bank would find it difficult to ignore such market signals entirely. Whether the rate-hiking cycle continues beyond January, however, will depend on inflation data released in the coming months. The outlook for asset markets will depend largely on the interaction between inflation and investment trends. If inflationary pressures ease as oil prices stabilize at lower levels while the investment cycle remains resilient, asset prices, including equities, could stage a strong rebound. Conversely, if inflation remains elevated while investment momentum weakens, concerns over an economic slowdown or recession could weigh on financial markets. Park expects inflationary pressures to ease gradually, given the prospect of lower and more stable oil prices. He also believes the investment cycle will remain resilient despite recent concerns, leaving open the possibility of an earlier-than-expected rebound in the stock market.

title: US PCE Inflation Reaches 3.8% as Core Prices Accelerate - cwibc.co.id
body: Rising underlying price pressures strengthened expectations of tighter monetary policy as US inflation accelerated in October 2026. The Commerce Department reported on Wednesday that the Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index increased 3.8% annually, while core PCE inflation reached 3.3%, adding pressure on the Federal Reserve ahead of its December policy meeting. The headline PCE index increased 0.3% month over month, slowing from 0.5% in September. Its annual rate rose from an upwardly revised 3.7% in September, matching economists' expectations. Core PCE, which excludes volatile food and energy prices, also increased 0.3% monthly. However, its annual rate accelerated from 3.1% to 3.3%, exceeding the 3.2% market forecast. The latest figures also showed that the three-month annualized inflation rate climbed to 3.6%, compared with an upwardly revised 3% previously, according to economist Bradley Saunders of Capital Economics. Saunders said the persistent strength in underlying inflation could influence the Federal Reserve's next decisions. He expects a quarter-percentage-point increase in December, while warning that another adjustment could follow in January. "The continued strength in core PCE inflation … makes a December rate hike certain. While we still think a 25bp hike is the most likely course of action at next month's meeting, the strength of the data means a follow-up hike in January could also be necessary," said Bradley Saunders, economist at Capital Economics. Price increases also appeared across goods and services. Core goods prices rose 0.35% month over month, nearly doubling their previous pace, while their annual inflation rate increased to 2.3% from 2%. Services prices advanced 0.28% monthly, with recreational services, food and accommodation services contributing to the increase. Energy prices also continued to influence broader price pressures. Mike Skordeles, head of US economics at Truist Advisory Services, offered a less concerning assessment of the report. He argued that comparisons with relatively weak inflation readings from the previous year made the latest annual figures appear stronger. Skordeles also expects this comparison effect to continue in November, noting that both headline and core inflation were below their longer-term trends during the corresponding period in 2025. "The overall inflation trajectory is largely unchanged, especially when excluding food and energy," said Mike Skordeles, head of US economics at Truist Advisory Services. Household income and spending data provided additional insight into economic conditions. Personal income increased 0.7% in October, accelerating from 0.3% in September, while personal spending growth slowed to 0.3% from 0.6%. Federal Reserve officials have also expressed differing views on the scale of further monetary tightening. Governor Chris Waller said a quarter-point increase in December should be accompanied by a signal of another increase of the same size in January. Alternatively, he indicated that a larger half-percentage-point adjustment in December could be considered. Governor Lisa Cook similarly argued that financial conditions remained too accommodative despite persistent inflation. She warned that delaying an increase could leave the central bank behind the curve, adding pressure for action at the December meeting.

title: Gold Falls Nearly 2% as US GDP Growth Accelerates - Demokratis.co.id
body: Stronger US economic growth and relatively stable inflation have pressured gold prices , pushing spot gold below a closely watched support level. The metal fell nearly 2% to $3,484.20 an ounce after revised third-quarter economic data showed stronger-than-expected expansion, according to the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA). The US economy grew at an annualized rate of 4.3% between July and September, significantly above the initial estimate of 3.4% and the 2.2% recorded in the second quarter. The revised figure also exceeded economists' consensus forecast of 3.5%. According to the BEA, stronger investment and consumer spending, alongside increased government spending, contributed to the expansion. These gains were partly offset by declining exports, while imports increased. The agency revised its initial GDP estimate upward by 0.9 percentage point, primarily reflecting stronger investment and consumer spending figures. Inflation indicators presented a relatively stable picture. The price index for gross domestic purchases increased 2.7% in the third quarter, down 0.3 percentage point from the previous estimate, according to the BEA. The personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index rose 2.1%, while the core PCE index, which excludes food and energy, increased 2.5%. Both figures remained unchanged from their initial estimates. A separate BEA report showed that monthly core PCE inflation increased 0.3% in October, matching economists' expectations. However, annual PCE inflation accelerated to 3.8% from 3.6% in September. Annual core PCE inflation also increased, reaching 3.3% in October compared with 3.1% in the previous month. These figures indicate that inflation remains elevated despite the absence of stronger monthly price increases than economists anticipated. The combination of solid economic growth and inflation data has provided little support for gold. Analysts have noted that inflation pressures are not accelerating, but the economic figures could give the Federal Reserve room to increase interest rates next month and in early 2027. Higher interest rates can weigh on gold prices by increasing the relative attractiveness of interest-bearing assets. Market attention has therefore remained focused on economic indicators that could influence the Federal Reserve's monetary policy decisions. Spot gold has struggled to maintain support above $3,500 an ounce following the stronger GDP figures and inflation readings. The latest reported price stood at $3,484.20 an ounce, representing a decline of nearly 2% for the day.

Become a Kalkine member today to get access to our research reports, in-depth technical and fundamental research. Learn More The Federal Reserve's policy outlook remains closely connected to the persistence of inflation in the American economy. A November address by New York Federal Reserve president John Williams identified the continuing need for progress towards price stability while acknowledging resilience in economic activity. The combination matters because monetary policy must consider developments in prices and employment rather than relying exclusively on one indicator. An economy capable of continuing to expand may still experience price pressures that require a restrictive policy setting, while changes in labour conditions can alter the balance of risks. Inflation measures changes in the general price level rather than an individual product's price. Particular items may become more expensive because of supply conditions, demand or changes in production and distribution costs. The policy question concerns the extent to which such movements contribute to persistent broader inflation. Williams identified inflation remaining too high relative to the Federal Reserve's price stability objective. Returning inflation sustainably to the desired level is distinct from recording a favourable result in a single reporting period. Policymakers consider a range of measures to assess the composition of price pressures. This can help identify whether changes are concentrated in particular categories or are becoming more widespread throughout the economy. The policy objective relates to the rate at which the general price level changes, rather than a requirement to reverse every increase in individual prices. A decline in inflation can therefore coexist with a price level that remains higher than it was earlier. That distinction matters when interpreting Williams's assessment. The persistence of inflation above the central bank's objective is relevant to the stance of monetary policy even when some individual categories have experienced periods of more moderate price growth. The composition of inflation also matters because different causes may have different implications for monetary policy. An increase in the cost of a particular imported input can raise the prices of products using that input. A more general increase in demand can place pressure on a broader range of prices and on available resources. These influences can occur at the same time. The central bank's task involves examining how individual changes affect the overall inflation process rather than assuming that each change has the same significance. Energy prices can affect consumers directly through fuel and utility costs. They can also influence businesses through transport, production and other operating expenses. The extent to which higher input costs translate into final prices depends partly on demand and the ability of businesses to absorb or pass through those costs. Changes in trade arrangements and the demand associated with technological development can also affect particular product categories. Williams discussed such developments in the context of the broader inflation assessment. The relevant distinction is whether price changes remain concentrated or begin to influence wage-setting, business pricing and expectations across a wider range of economic activity. Different patterns can have different implications for monetary policy. Williams also discussed the influence of tariffs and demand connected with artificial intelligence on prices in particular areas of the economy. Tariffs can affect the cost of imported goods or inputs, while expansion in computing infrastructure can increase demand for the resources required to build and operate it. title: SBI Economists Warn 50-Basis-Point RBI Rate Hike Could Hurt Financial Stability And Economic Growth - Free Press Journal
body: SBI economists favour a 25-basis-point RBI rate hike in December, citing financial stability risks | AI Representational Image Mumbai, November 24, 2026: SBI economists on Tuesday opined that “financial stability” concerns led them to cut their rate hike expectation to 0.25 per cent at the next RBI policy review from the earlier projection of 0.50 per cent. A jumbo rate hike risks investment outflows, rupee instability and an impact on economic growth, they said in a report. “The RBI should be mindfully cognisant about financial stability amidst the call for a jumbo rate hike of 0.50 per cent in the December policy,” the note said. “A rate hike of 0.25 per cent should be enough given the inflation trajectory rather than recourse to a jumbo one that might unleash reverse causation of capital outflows, rupee instability and, of course, growth concerns,” it added. It can be recalled that economists at SBI had estimated a 0.50 per cent rate hike in December, after the last policy review in October, when the six-member rate-setting panel hiked the key rates by 0.25 per cent and also shifted the policy stance to “calibrated tightening” from “neutral” earlier. In an earlier report on November 12, State Bank of India’s Economic Research Department had revised its forecast for the RBI’s December monetary policy, expecting a 0.25 per cent rate hike instead of its earlier projection of 0.50 per cent. This was due to improved external conditions, a revival in foreign fund inflows and easing pressure on the rupee. The October hike was the first such move in nearly four years, and the RBI had also signalled that further rate hikes could follow amid rising inflation, a weak rupee and high crude oil prices. The RBI’s Monetary Policy Committee is scheduled to meet between December 2 and December 4 to decide on the policy interest rate. On the global front, the SBI report said that the US Federal Reserve is likely to keep rates unchanged in the December policy. Following the recent equity-market sell-off, expectations of a more aggressive 50-basis-point increase have largely receded, while the probability of the Fed maintaining rates has edged up to around 10 per cent, the report said. The sharp correction in equity markets and the possibility of a slowdown in economic activity could complicate the Fed’s policy decision. The yields on 10-year G-sec are witnessing a declining trend and are currently hovering around 4.96 per cent. “We believe that the yields are likely to touch towards 4.75 per cent,” the SBI report said. title: Fed’s Inflation Gauge Hits 3.8% as Strong Growth Adds Pressure for December Rate Hike - Business Times
body: US inflation accelerated in October as the Federal Reserve's preferred price gauge rose 3.8% from a year earlier, while stronger economic growth reinforced expectations of a December interest-rate increase and complicated the central bank's outlook for 2027. The personal consumption expenditures price index increased from September's 3.7% annual rate, the Commerce Department reported Wednesday. Core inflation, which excludes food and energy, climbed to 3.3% from 3.1%, reaching its highest level since November 2023. The headline reading matched the Dow Jones consensus forecast, while core inflation exceeded expectations by 0.1 percentage point, CNBC reported. Both measures increased 0.3% from the previous month. Markets continued to fully price in a quarter-percentage-point rate increase at the Fed's Dec. 8-9 meeting. Inflation has remained above the central bank's 2% target for roughly five and a half years. "Inflation is too hot and it will not be brought under control as long as economic demand is also too hot," said Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds. A separate Commerce Department release showed gross domestic product expanded at a revised 4.3% annualized pace in the third quarter. Upward revisions to investment, consumer spending and government expenditures strengthened the picture of an economy maintaining substantial momentum despite tighter monetary policy. Consumer spending grew 4.2% during the quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, a measure Fed officials monitor for underlying demand, increased 5.8%, an upward revision of 0.9 percentage point. October household spending offered a more subdued signal. Nominal expenditures rose 0.3%, slightly below expectations, while inflation-adjusted spending was essentially unchanged. Personal income increased 0.7%, exceeding the 0.4% forecast. The Bureau of Economic Analysis attributed the gain primarily to compensation, government social benefits and asset income, with one-time Medicare Improvement Fund premium rebates contributing to the increase in benefits. Disposable income rose 0.8% before inflation and 0.5% after adjusting for prices. With income outpacing spending, the personal saving rate increased to 4.1% from September's revised 3.6%. Stock-index futures extended losses after the releases, while Treasury yields fell sharply. Expectations for 2027 rate increases nevertheless eased somewhat: traders still priced in two hikes but reduced the probability of a third to approximately one-third from about 50% Tuesday, according to CME Group's FedWatch tool. The inflation figures arrive as policymakers assess pressures from the Iran war, tariffs and demand associated with artificial intelligence investment. The White House announced additional tariffs Wednesday covering 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union and Japan. While tariffs and supply disruptions can produce temporary price increases, some policymakers worry their effects could spread and become persistent. "America's inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. Labor-market data also showed continued resilience. Initial unemployment claims fell 13,000 to 189,000 in the week ended Nov. 21, below the 200,000 forecast and near their lowest levels since the late 1960s, the Labor Department reported.

body: On November 25, surging credit risk metrics across the AI industry—highlighted by CoreWeave’s 70% implied default probability and record-high CDS costs for Nvidia, Alphabet, Oracle, and SpaceX—reflect growing investor concern over whether massive capital expenditures on data centers and chips will generate sufficient cash flow to cover debt costs. As financing pressures mount, market scrutiny is shifting from pure revenue growth to free cash flow and balance sheet health. This is driving valuation contractions and widening divergence between cash-rich tech giants and emerging cloud providers heavily reliant on external debt. TradingKey - Pressure from the artificial intelligence investment boom is spreading from the stock market to the credit market. As tech companies pour vast amounts of capital into data centers, chips, and power infrastructure, investors are beginning to reassess whether these projects can generate sufficient cash flow to cover debt costs. On November 25, CoreWeave ( CRWV ) and Nvidia ( NVDA ) saw credit risk metrics rise to historic highs. Alphabet ( GOOGL ), Oracle ( ORCL ), and SpaceX ( SPCX ) also saw five-year credit default swap costs hit record highs, indicating that market concerns have spread from highly leveraged new cloud computing companies to the broader AI industry chain. According to data from ICE Data Services, the annualized cost of five-year default protection on CoreWeave's debt rose by as much as 2.09 percentage points to reach 15.34 percentage points, marking its largest single-day increase on record. Based on swap market pricing, the implied probability of CoreWeave experiencing a credit event over the next five years has exceeded 70%. A CDS is essentially a credit risk protection instrument through which investors pay a fee to receive compensation if the debt issuer experiences a specified credit event. Typically, higher CDS costs indicate that the market perceives greater risk in the underlying debt or demands higher risk compensation. Therefore, the sharp rise in CoreWeave's CDS prices reflects deepening investor concerns over its debt-servicing capacity and future financing conditions. The reason the market is particularly sensitive to CoreWeave relates to the scale of funding required for its business expansion. As an AI computing infrastructure provider, the company needs to continuously invest resources to meet customers' computing demands. When the market begins questioning the return on investment from AI buildouts, investors naturally reassess the debt levels, cash flows, and refinancing capabilities of such companies. If financing costs continue to rise, the difficulty of expanding computing scale in the future could also increase for the company. Even more concerning is that credit market stress is no longer confined to CoreWeave. CDS spreads for Nvidia, Google, Oracle, and SpaceX also hit record highs on Wednesday, indicating that investors are reassessing the credit risks of companies tied to the AI supply chain. Meanwhile, the spread on the US investment-grade CDX index widened by as much as 3.1 basis points to 65.63 basis points, reaching its highest intraday level since March 31, while risk indicators in the high-yield bond market also weakened. Neocloud companies borrow funds to purchase Nvidia chips and then repay debt with GPU leasing revenue, while Nvidia expands its customers' purchasing capacity through investments, partnerships, or other forms of support. As long as GPU utilization rates remain high, leasing prices stay stable, and customer contracts are honored, this model can sustain rapid growth. body: The actual buying will be very small. At index weight, EZPZ's HYPE position should be worth well under $1 million, so there's no direct effect on the token, on bitcoin or ether, or on crypto equities such as COIN and MSTR. The real effect is on credibility. HYPE now has a place in a third diversified index product, which strengthens its claim to be a large-cap asset alongside XRP and Solana. That matters for future index rebalances and for advisers who only buy through ETFs. Sentiment is the counterweight: the dedicated HYPE ETFs have had recent outflows, and the token is about 28% below its late-August level. Investors are watching more than they are buying. Another big fund manager is making room for Hyperliquid, but the amount involved is tiny and the token's price is going the other way. Franklin Templeton's Franklin Crypto Index ETF (EZPZ) will start holding Hyperliquid's HYPE token on or around December 1, according to a prospectus supplement filed with the US Securities and Exchange Commission on November 25. HYPE will be the only new name in the fund's lineup, taking it to eight assets alongside bitcoin, ether, XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, Cardano and Stellar. The change follows a November 16 notice from CF Benchmarks naming HYPE as the sole new constituent of its Institutional Digital Asset Index, which EZPZ tracks. The fund holds each asset at roughly its index weight and rebalances quarterly, so buying HYPE is an automatic index step, not a decision by Franklin. The filing does not disclose HYPE's starting weight. Scale matters here. EZPZ had about $17.02 million in net assets at the end of September, with bitcoin making up around 76% of the portfolio and ether close to 13%, according to fund data cited by crypto.news. As a rough illustration, a weight similar to the 3.36% HYPE received in Hashdex's Nasdaq CME Crypto Index ETF (NCIQ) in September would amount to only around $600,000 of the token. The addition shows where index products are heading. It won't add meaningful demand. Index adoption is spreading. Hashdex added HYPE to NCIQ from September 1, and the Bitwise 10 Crypto Index ETF added it in July. Three US spot HYPE ETFs launched this year now hold under $250 million in assets between them, The Block reported. Cumulative inflows into HYPE ETFs have topped $259 million despite a recent stretch of outflows. The price has not kept pace with the institutional interest. HYPE traded around $60 on November 25, well below the roughly $83 it fetched when Hashdex's inclusion was announced in late August. Even so, The Block reports the token is still up more than 120% on the year and ranks among the 10 largest cryptocurrencies, with a market value of about $13.6 billion. Regulation is the bigger thread. CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said on November 19 that onchain platforms like Hyperliquid can reach US retail users either by partnering with an existing exchange or by obtaining their own. Payward, Kraken's parent company, is already pursuing a partnership route for decentralized derivatives venues. The next things to watch are HYPE's disclosed weight once EZPZ rebalances, whether flows into the dedicated HYPE ETFs turn positive again, and any concrete step by Hyperliquid toward a licensed US channel. title: German consumer confidence remains in the doldrums heading into December
summary: Germany December GfK consumer confidence -30.2 vs -29.9 expected Prior -30.8; revised to -30.9 German consumer sentiment edged up heading into December but continues to remain subdued as a whole, according to the latest GfK/NIM survey. The breakdown shows that economic expectations falling to -1.6 from 2.1 while price expectations also nudged up a little to 2.8 from 1.0 previously. THe only real bright spot is that income expectations improved a little to -13.9 from -15.7 before this. But at the balance, the report is still suggesting that consumer confidence remains in the dumps. GfK/NIM even noted that the index was "more or less stagnating at a low level" and that doesn't bode well ahead of the Christmas shopping season. If anything else, this does provide some suggestion to the ECB that the euro area's largest economy is still not exactly recovering all too well despite the more resilient showing in the first half of the year. The second half of the year looks to be one of consolidating and stagnating momentum, which isn't the most ideal situation as inflation pressures remain strong. For now, policymakers may still get away with another rate hike, or perhaps even two, but the challenge will grow to be greater next year amid higher stagflationary risks potentially. Just as things were starting to get interesting again after yesterday's impressive recovery, US traders are now off to enjoy their Thanksgiving break. As a reminder, US stock and bond markets will be closed today in observance of Thanksgiving. And even though trading resumes tomorrow, Wall Street will only be open until 1800 GMT (1pm ET) while the bond market will wrap things up at 1900 GMT (2pm ET). But in reality, many market participants will already have one foot out the door until Monday. So, one can reasonably expect thinner liquidity conditions across broader markets over the next two days - especially during US trading hours. That being said, let's not mistake a lack of liquidity for a lack of volatility. With fewer buyers and sellers around, it takes considerably less money to move markets. Any relatively modest order size or unexpected headlines could make for some rather exaggerated moves in currencies, gold and stock futures. And given how fragile the market sentiment is looking this week, I'd be particularly wary of reading too much into any technical breakouts or breakdowns during the coming two days. As much as the turnaround yesterday was quite encouraging, the real test for dip buyers will be whether they can continue to build on that momentum once the usual crowd returns next week. All eyes will be on tech stocks to see if they can sustain a more meaningful recovery from here, or is this just another half-hearted attempt at buying the dip like we saw on Monday? In any case, we will have to wait until the start of next week to have better clarity on all of that. In the meantime, just remember that you are not obliged to chase every move on your screen. The next two days could offer some trading opportunities but they could just as easily serve up a few nasty traps. So, be careful out there. At times, following the market in enjoying a little time off isn't such a bad idea. As mentioned earlier this week, there will always be another opportunity to make money in markets. body: Asian stocks extended their recovery on Thursday, led by chipmakers, as two of the region's central banks struck hawkish tones and US stock futures rose in thin trade with Wall Street closed for Thanksgiving. Japan's Nikkei 225 rose about 1.6% to around 57,900, adding to its early gains, while the broader Topix rose about 0.5%. South Korea's Kospi climbed about 1.5% and the tech-heavy Kosdaq more than 2%, as SK Hynix gained about 3.5% and Samsung Electronics about 1.7%. The moves recovered part of Wednesday's heavy losses, when the Kospi fell more than 6%. In China, Hong Kong's Hang Seng rose about 1.9%, while the Shanghai Composite was little changed. US stock index futures built on Wall Street's late rebound on Wednesday, with S&P 500 futures up about 0.7% and Nasdaq 100 futures about 1.1% higher. The Bank of Korea raised its base rate by a quarter point to 3.25%, its third hike since July, as expected. The decision drew two dissents, from board members Lee Soo-hyung and Hwang Kun-il, but the board's projections leaned hawkish: 15 of 21 put the rate above 3.25% in six months, including seven at 3.75%. The bank said inflation will stay above target for a prolonged period and that the timing of further hikes will depend on inflation, growth and financial stability. It forecast growth of 3.9% this year and 4.1% in 2027, driven by semiconductor exports. In Japan, Bank of Japan board member Naoki Tamura said the policy rate should be brought to neutral "soon", repeating his view that neutral is around 2%, well above the current 1.25%. He said the BoJ should "make haste slowly" but be ready to speed up hikes if inflation overshoots. Japanese two-year government bond yields rose about 4 basis points to around 1.76%, while the 10-year yield edged up to around 2.66%. The yen barely moved, with USD/JPY holding near 159.10. Australian private capital spending jumped 12.2% in the third quarter, almost three times the 4.4% forecast, as equipment investment surged 23.1% to a record, led by the industry that includes data centres. Firms also lifted their spending plans for 2026-27 by 11.8% to about A$224 billion. The Australian dollar rose about 0.3% to around 0.6646. S&P Global Ratings placed Nvidia's AA rating on CreditWatch negative, warning of a possible one-notch downgrade within 90 days over concerns about board independence, key-person risk and export-control questions. Moody's, by contrast, kept its Aa1 rating and stable outlook. Elsewhere, CoreWeave's banks are preparing a $4.5 billion loan backed by a Meta contract, even as the cost of insuring CoreWeave's own debt hit a record. South Africa's central bank warned that AI firms now compete with governments for long-term funding. Resistance to data centre projects is spreading too, from Tokyo's suburbs to Australia's Northern Territory and across the United States. Sentiment calls were mixed. Citi Wealth said extreme investor fear offers a buying opportunity, Bank of America set a cautious S&P 500 target of 7,800 for the end of 2027, and Goldman Sachs said hedge funds have been adding short positions. Michael Burry closed his remaining bearish bets on the Nasdaq-100 but said he still plans to short Nvidia nearer $200. Gold held near $3,590 an ounce after Wednesday's sharp reversal from a 14-month low near $3,425, while Ray Dalio's recommendation of a 10% to 15% gold allocation drew renewed attention. Silver rose about 1.2%. Brent crude traded around $91 a barrel after a tanker reported a nearby explosion from an unknown projectile 50 nautical miles west of Dubai late on Wednesday, the latest in a string of attacks on Gulf shipping. Bitcoin rose about 3% to around $61,000. US stock and bond markets are closed for Thanksgiving, and Friday is a shortened session. Thin liquidity may keep moves exaggerated into the weekend. body: Libya Plans New Oil Bidding Rounds Despite Mounting Security Risks What I Cover Irina Slav has been writing about global energy markets since 2007, covering the oil and gas industry, energy security, commodities, and the… Libya has scheduled a bidding round for discovered but undeveloped oil fields in 2027, and another one in 2028 focused on exploration, as it seeks to ramp up oil production despite the unstable security situation. The National Oil Corporation last held a tender for undeveloped oil fields in 2025, the first in 18 years, and last year it awarded five of a total of 22 blocks on offer to companies including Chevron, Eni, Repsol, and QatarEnergy. Bidders also included Exxon and TotalEnergies, completing the wide representation of Big Oil. Earlier this year, NOC and Austria’s OMV declared the Essar discovery commercially viable, with reserves estimated at 195 million barrels of oil from the upper and lower “Sabil” reservoirs, with an expected production capacity of about 5,000 barrels per day, the Libyan state oil firm said in July. Libya’s National Oil Corporation currently pumps around 1.4 million bpd to 1.5 million bpd, but ambitions are set high, with NOC eyeing output rates of over 2 million barrels daily by 2030. However, security remains a big problem, with various factions using oil fields, export terminals, and pipelines as bargaining chips against other factions. Temporary field closures and export suspensions have become a fixture in the North African country, as this or that group takes control of a pipeline or a field and makes demands to the government. Just this week, Libya’s oil production crashed by about 350,000 barrels per day after an outlaw group closed a valve on the pipeline transporting crude oil from Sharara, the country’s biggest oilfield, the National Oil Corporation said on Monday. body: Libya Plans New Oil Bidding Rounds Despite Mounting Security Risks What I Cover Irina Slav has been writing about global energy markets since 2007, covering the oil and gas industry, energy security, commodities, and the… Canada’s Enbridge is reportedly in talks with a group of Indigenous communities for the sale of a stake in its Line 3 pipeline network, according to the Globe and Mail , which cited unnamed sources. The sale could fetch over $1 billion (C$1.5 billion), the publication also said, adding that this would make it the largest transaction involving indigenous communities in the country. The size of the stake to be sold is 6%, the report also said. The Line 3 pipeline system has a capacity of some 760,000 barrels of crude daily, linking Alberta’s oil sands to Wisconsin. It is part of Enbridge’s larger network of pipelines that can carry up to 3.2 million barrels of crude oil daily. Enbridge is “currently exploring financial partnerships across numerous assets where the economics are favourable for the Indigenous partners and our business,” a spokesman for the company told the Globe and Mail in a written response to a request for comment on the information. Earlier this year, Enbridge made two transactions that boosted its total network, both in the United States. In August, the company announced the acquisition of Salt Creek Midstream’s crude oil gathering business, strengthening the pipeline giant’s ability to move barrels from the Delaware Basin to export markets on the U.S. Gulf Coast. A month later, Enbridge struck a deal to buy Tallgrass Energy’s crude transportation business for $2.55 billion in cash, adding major pipeline and storage assets connecting U.S. Rockies production with the Cushing, Oklahoma, oil hub. The transaction , announced in September, included a 75% interest in the 1,050-mile Pony Express Pipeline, which has a capacity of roughly 460,000 barrels per day and links Rockies crude production with Cushing and around 500,000 bpd of refining capacity. Enbridge will also acquire a 51% interest in the Powder River Gateway system, which includes two pipelines with combined capacity of about 240,000 bpd, as well as approximately 8.4 million barrels of crude storage across nine terminals. body: Enbridge Eyes $1 Billion Pipeline Deal With Indigenous Communities What I Cover Irina Slav has been writing about global energy markets since 2007, covering the oil and gas industry, energy security, commodities, and the… Crude oil prices bounced back in early Asian trade on Thursday, climbing higher after fresh reports of tankers hitting mines in the Strait of Hormuz and the latest Yemeni Houthi attack on Saudi Arabia, which targeted a refinery. At the time of writing, Brent crude was trading at $95.30 per barrel, with West Texas Intermediate at $84.36 per barrel. The rise follows several days of losses as traders focused on predictions of a supply overhang, ignoring the mine strike reports. However, the frequency of these reports, coupled with data showing the average daily flow of energy commodities out of Hormuz, seems to have broken through the glut wall, pushing prices higher. Iranian state media reports of tankers hitting mines in Hormuz have become a daily occurrence recently, with some days seeing more than one incident, prompting tanker tracking firms such as Kpler to report a decline in daily average flows of crude out of the Persian Gulf. These reports are undermining the glut story, showing that exports of crude from the region are still—or once again—significantly lower than they were before the United States and Israel first attacked Iran at the end of February. The Houthi attack on Ras Tanura, the largest refinery in Saudi Arabia, contributed to the change in trader perception, a reminder that there is a war in the Middle East and the prospect of peace remains quite remote. The Ras Tanura refinery is located on Saudi Arabia’s eastern coast, on the Persian Gulf, and is part of a major oil export hub. “The broadening of the Middle East conflict threatens to halt the recovery in oil flows in recent weeks. Persian Gulf crude exports rose last week but remain on a declining trend,” ANZ analyst Daniel Hynes said, as cited by Reuters. title: Gold draws buying while copper sees outflows as both ETFs plunge around 20% - 머니투데이
body: Gold draws buying while copper sees outflows as both ETFs plunge around 20% Gold and copper prices have fallen in tandem, dragging down returns on related exchange-traded funds (ETFs). However, investor sentiment toward the two metals has diverged. Gold ETFs are attracting bargain-hunting money, while copper ETFs are seeing funds flow out. According to Koscom's ETF Check on Nov. 26, the three-month return on ACE KRX Physical Gold, based on reinvested distributions, stood at minus 27.13 percent as of the previous day. Other gold ETFs, including TIGER KRX Physical Gold (minus 26.93 percent), TIGER Gold Futures (H) (minus 24.71 percent) and KODEX Gold Futures (H) (minus 24.33 percent), also posted losses in the 20 percent range. ETFs investing in copper, another major commodity, fared similarly. As of the previous day, KODEX Copper Futures (H) and TIGER Physical Copper had posted three-month returns of minus 22.38 percent and minus 21.75 percent, respectively. Expectations of further U.S. interest rate hikes are cited as a key factor behind the recent decline in commodity prices. "Slower growth in liquidity and a stronger dollar have increased selling pressure across commodity markets," said Park Ju-ran, an analyst at Samsung Securities. "Growing doubts about the AI industry, which has led gains in asset markets, have also raised concerns that an economic slowdown could weaken demand for metals." Despite similarly weak returns, fund flows moved in opposite directions. A total of 74.8 billion won flowed into seven gold-themed ETFs over the past three months, while 21.1 billion won flowed out of two copper-themed ETFs. Gold is still considered attractive as a medium- to long-term investment, partly because central banks, major buyers of the metal, are increasing their purchases. Investors also appear to be taking advantage of lower prices to buy gold. According to Samsung Futures, estimates by the World Gold Council (WGC) show that net gold purchases by central banks worldwide rose from 58 tons in the first quarter to 296 tons in the second quarter and 321 tons in the third quarter. The third-quarter figure was the highest since the fourth quarter of 2024. Copper, meanwhile, has come under pressure from growing doubts about the growth prospects of the AI industry, which had helped drive prices higher. Demand for copper from traditional industries such as construction and manufacturing has remained stagnant over the past three years. However, expectations had been widespread that the expansion of AI data centers would boost demand for power grids and drive up copper prices, as the metal is a key material used in power cables. The outlook shifted after the Democratic Party won decisively in the U.S. midterm elections on a platform that included tighter regulations on data center construction. LS Securities estimated that if concerns over data center construction delays materialize, copper demand in 2029 could be about 450,000 tons lower than previously forecast. Securities analysts expect gold prices to remain weak for the time being. Samsung Futures forecast an average gold price of $3,800 per ounce next year, 13.6 percent below its projection for this year. "Interest rates will continue to cap gold prices until June next year, when the end of rate hikes is expected to become clear," said Ok Ji-hoe, a researcher at Samsung Futures. "Gold prices are expected to bottom out toward the end of the second quarter and rebound in the second half as expectations of rate cuts take shape." Copper is also unlikely to regain upward momentum until uncertainty surrounding AI investment subsides, analysts say. "As price movements have become more closely correlated with financial markets, a recovery in investor sentiment toward the AI industry and U.S. technology stocks, which have supported the optimistic outlook for medium- to long-term demand, is needed for prices to rebound," Park said. The gold-silver ratio is currently 85.8 — one ounce of gold is worth the same as 85.8 ounces of silver. The gold-silver ratio is the oldest relative-value measure in precious metals: it simply divides the gold price by the silver price. For most of monetary history the ratio was fixed near 15:1; in the modern free-market era it has ranged widely — from below 20 to above 100 — moving as the two metals respond differently to industrial cycles and investment flows. Traders watch the ratio as a gauge of how the two metals are priced relative to each other and to their own history. A rising ratio means gold is outperforming silver; a falling ratio means silver is gaining ground. The ratio above is calculated live from the same spot quotes shown on this page and on our gold price page . The spot price is the market price for one troy ounce of silver for immediate delivery, quoted in U.S. dollars. It is derived from the most actively traded silver futures contract together with over-the-counter dealing, and it moves nearly around the clock as trading follows the sun from New York to London, Zurich, Shanghai and Hong Kong. A troy ounce is 31.1034768 grams — about 10% heavier than the avoirdupois ounce used for groceries. Physical silver products trade at a premium above spot that covers fabrication and distribution — and because silver is far less valuable per gram than gold, the premium is proportionally larger: minting a one-ounce silver coin costs nearly as much as minting a gold one, but represents a much bigger share of the metal’s value. The spot price is for silver delivered now; a futures price is for silver delivered on a set date in the future, traded on exchanges such as COMEX. The two normally differ by the cost of carrying silver to that date — storage, insurance and interest — which is why futures usually trade slightly above spot ( contango ). When futures trade below spot ( backwardation ), it signals unusually strong demand for immediate physical delivery. The price on this page is the spot price; quotes for "silver futures" refer to the most active COMEX contract. Monetary forces: rates, the dollar, and gold. title: Bitcoin (BTC) Price Prediction: Oversold bounce attempt meets a heavy overhead supply wall - Blockchain News
body: Bitcoin was trading at $60,545.48, up 2.30% over 24 hours, after a session range of $57,300.38 to $61,622.38. The setup is therefore less a clean trend reversal than an oversold rebound attempt inside a broader downtrend. The daily RSI at 27.57 signals oversold conditions, which helps explain the bounce, but the MACD remains negative and the histogram is flat at 0.0000, indicating momentum has not yet turned decisively higher. The moving-average structure also shows BTC sitting deeply discounted versus its 20-day average, which supports a mean-reversion case but does not confirm it. Recent news flow has not been kind to the asset. CoinDesk reported on November 24 that U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shed $570 million in a fifth straight day of outflows, lifting the month’s cumulative outflows to a record $4.71 billion. The same report said bitcoin had slipped back toward $60,000 after an intraday push above $64,000. That matters because it links the spot tape to a persistent withdrawal of supporting flow, rather than to a one-off headline move. The Block added on November 25 that bitcoin fell below $58,000 before recovering, with CoinShares’ James Butterfill saying he thinks bitcoin may be near the “tail end of the bear market” and sees the coin trading between $60,000 and $90,000, with a breakout likely tied to a change in Fed expectations. That weakens the signal: a low-volume rebound can work, but it usually needs follow-through from heavier turnover before traders treat it as durable. That matters because funding alone does not tell you whether market participants are aggressively bullish or bearish; it only says the perpetual swap market is not paying a strong premium to be long at this moment. Citi’s November 18 target cut to $99,532 is still above spot, but the relevance is not the upside figure itself. If BTC can reclaim $62,345.11 and hold above the $59,822.75 pivot on improving volume, the market can start testing whether the current move is a genuine rebound rather than a dead-cat bounce. title: US Inflation Climbs to 3.8% as Fed Faces Rate Decision - cwibc.co.id
body: Rising consumer prices are creating a tougher policy challenge for the Federal Reserve as US inflation accelerated in October, reaching nearly twice the central bank's 2% target. The Commerce Department reported the increase on Wednesday, raising concerns about further interest rate adjustments and the inflation outlook for 2027. The personal consumption expenditures price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation measure, increased at a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 3.8%. That matched the Dow Jones consensus forecast but represented a 0.1 percentage point increase from September. Core PCE inflation, which excludes food and energy prices, reached 3.3%, according to the Commerce Department. The figure exceeded economists' expectations by 0.1 percentage point. Although policymakers officially follow headline PCE, they consider the core measure a more reliable indicator of longer-term inflation trends. Separate economic data showed that US gross domestic product expanded at an annualized rate of 4.3% in the third quarter, based on a revised Commerce Department estimate. The upward revision reflected stronger investment, consumer spending and government expenditure. Consumer spending, which represents approximately two-thirds of economic activity, increased 4.2% during the third quarter. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers, a measure closely monitored by Federal Reserve officials as an indicator of underlying demand, climbed 5.8%, following an upward revision of 0.9 percentage point. Monthly consumer spending increased 0.3%, matching the pace of price increases but falling 0.1 percentage point short of forecasts. Personal income rose 0.7%, exceeding the 0.4% estimate, while the personal saving rate reached 4.1%. Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds, highlighted the relationship between economic demand and persistent price pressures. "Inflation is too hot and it will not be brought under control as long as economic demand is also too hot," said Chris Rupkey, chief economist at Fwdbonds. Inflation pressures have been reinforced by several factors, including tariffs, energy costs and strong demand associated with the expansion of artificial intelligence infrastructure. The late-February attacks on Iran led by the US and Israel also preceded a renewed increase in inflation. The White House announced another round of tariffs on Wednesday covering 14 trading partners, including China, the European Union and Japan. While policymakers generally regard supply disruptions and tariffs as temporary pressures, concerns have grown that their effects could spread across the broader economy. Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union, said inflationary pressures extend beyond energy market disruptions. "America's inflation problem is bigger than an energy shock," said Heather Long, chief economist at Navy Federal Credit Union. Financial markets showed mixed reactions following the economic releases. Stock futures extended their losses, while Treasury yields also moved sharply lower. Market expectations for additional Federal Reserve rate increases in 2027 eased slightly, although two further increases remained priced in. Expectations for a third increase fell to approximately one in three, compared with an even chance on Tuesday. Markets had fully priced in a 0.25 percentage point interest rate increase at the Federal Reserve's December 8-9 meeting. The larger question remains how much additional tightening policymakers may need to bring inflation back to their 2% target. Inflation has remained above that objective for approximately 5.5 years. Meanwhile, the Labor Department reported that initial unemployment claims declined to 189,000 for the week ending November 21. That represented a decrease of 13,000 from the previous week and was close to the lowest level recorded since the late 1960s. Economists had expected 200,000 claims.

title: Nvidia Wins Back Wall Street Backing As Jensen Huang Returns; CRWD, LI Stocks Score Upgrades While DKNG, AMBA Face Pressure - TradingView
body: Nvidia Corp. (NVDA) quickly won back Wall Street bulls after its board reinstated Jensen Huang as CEO, while CrowdStrike (CRWD) received two ‘Buy’ upgrades this week. Ambarella (AMBA), DraftKings (DKNG) and Insmed (INSM) drew downgrades, and Li Auto (LI) got a rare, welcome lift from JPMorgan after a third-quarter beat. Eleven days ago, analysts were bracing for the worst. Now, with Huang back as President, CEO and board member, the firms that stepped aside are stepping back in. Bernstein upgraded Nvidia stock to ‘Outperform’ from ‘Market Perform’ and left its price target at $200. The firm had downgraded the stock when Huang's conduct looked likely to cost him his job, and it cut its target in half. The exit came the next day. Huang's departure was the main reason for the downgrade, the analyst said, so his return undoes it. Bernstein still stays positive on the AI buildout. Valuation with Huang at the helm "seems supportive enough to us for now," said the analyst. Oppenheimer's Rick Schafer upgraded the stock to “Outperform” from “Perform” with a $250 target. He called Huang's return a "win for AI and a win for investors" and said it lifts a "major cloud of uncertainty." StoneX went furthest, upgrading to “Buy” from “Hold” with a $270 target. The firm said Huang’s return addresses five issues: the pace of the roadmap, industry relationships, willingness to back the AI buildout, organizational structure and the likely retention of key talent. Guggenheim upgraded CrowdStrike stock to “Buy” from “Neutral” with a $280 target, implying 33% upside. The firm expects "hyper growth and profit." The analyst noted that CrowdStrike works closely with every hyperscaler, even Microsoft, which some investors not long ago saw as a threat to the company's survival. Deutsche Bank's Brad Zelnick also upgraded CRWD to “Buy” from “Hold”, raising his target to $300 from $240. His argument is that the market hasn't fully priced in how much AI will expand the cybersecurity opportunity. He calls CrowdStrike the leader in the space and thinks its $565 billion total addressable market estimate for 2034 will prove conservative given the "tsunami of cyber demand materializing as the AI frontier advances." JPMorgan's Nick Lai upgraded Li Auto to “Neutral” from “Underweight” and nudged his target to $10 from $9. The catalyst was "a clean beat" in Q3, driven mostly by a better product mix and cost efficiency. The firm still expects a cautious industry backdrop into 2027 to weigh on profit. On Wednesday, Li posted its first earnings beat in three quarters. BofA cut Ambarella stock’s rating to “Underperform” from “Neutral” and slashed its target to $30 from $70. Q3 results landed at the low end of guidance, and Q4 outlook came in below consensus. The analyst thinks investors will struggle to underwrite a growth inflection with memory allocation uncertain and AI memory demand strong. DraftKings stock lost an “Overweight” at Morgan Stanley, where Stephen Grambling moved it to “Equal Weight” and lowered his target to $23 from $31. The multiple has compressed and estimates have fallen, he said, because marketing costs are higher again. He argued that visibility and risk-adjusted returns both erode as the company ramps its prediction markets investment. Insmed stock drew two downgrades from Truist and BMO Capital, both tied to Sanofi's (SNY) deal to acquire the company for $175 per share, a roughly $41 billion transaction.
